issues.t: Spark plug blown out of the cylinder head
issues.eng: 5.4L V8 and 6.8L V10 Triton gas engines
issues.sym: A sudden loud popping or ticking noise, a rough-running engine with a misfire light, and sometimes an ignition coil sitting loose on top of the engine.
issues.why: These aluminum heads hold each spark plug with only a few threads. Over time a plug can loosen and strip them, and the plug gets pushed out of the head.
issues.next: Stop driving if a sudden loud tick and misfire appear. A shop can repair the threads with an insert. Make sure plugs are torqued correctly at every tune-up.

issues.t: Oil cooler and EGR cooler failure leading to head gasket trouble
issues.sym: White, sweet-smelling exhaust smoke, a coolant level that keeps dropping with no visible leak, pressure or bubbles in the coolant bottle, and overheating when towing.
issues.why: The engine oil cooler can clog inside, cutting coolant flow to the EGR cooler, which then overheats and ruptures. The resulting coolant loss and pressure can blow head gaskets on this engine.
issues.next: Stop towing and have a diesel shop compare oil and coolant temperatures and pressure-test the cooling system. Catching a clogged oil cooler early can prevent a much larger head gasket job.

issues.t: Injector control module (FICM) and injector failures
issues.sym: Hard or long cranking, especially when cold, rough idle, misfires, smoke, and loss of power.
issues.why: The module that powers the injectors can fail, often from low battery voltage, and the injectors themselves are a known failure point on this engine.
issues.next: Have the batteries and the module's output voltage tested before replacing injectors. Keep up with oil and fuel filter changes.

issues.t: Turbocharger vanes sticking from soot
issues.sym: Sluggish response from a stop, a lack of boost, or surging power, sometimes with a check engine light.
issues.why: Soot builds up in the variable-vane turbocharger and makes the vanes stick, so boost is not controlled properly.
issues.next: Have a diesel shop check boost control and clean or service the turbo. Regular highway driving and towing help keep soot down.

issues.t: Radiator leaks, EGR cooler failure and fuel in the oil
issues.sym: Coolant drips or crusty residue at the radiator, a falling coolant level, white smoke, overheating, or an oil level that rises or smells of fuel.
issues.why: The factory radiator is prone to cracking, the EGR coolers wear out, and the extra fuel used to clean the particulate filter can wash past the piston rings and thin the oil.
issues.next: Watch the coolant level and oil dipstick closely. Have leaks fixed promptly, and change the oil early if it smells of fuel. Stop driving if the engine overheats.

issues.t: Violent front-end shake ('death wobble')
issues.sym: After hitting a bump at highway speed on a 4x4, the steering wheel and front end shake hard side to side until you slow way down.
issues.why: The solid front axle relies on a track bar, tie rods, ball joints and a steering damper. Wear or looseness in any of these lets the front wheels start oscillating. Ford issued a service bulletin for 2017-2019 trucks that replaces the steering damper.
issues.next: Slow down gently without slamming the brakes when it happens, and have the front steering and suspension inspected before highway driving. A new damper alone can hide a worn part.

issues.t: High-pressure fuel pump failure
issues.sym: Sudden loss of power, the engine shutting off while driving, hard starting or no-start, sometimes with fuel-pressure codes.
issues.why: The high-pressure fuel pump can wear internally and shed metal into the fuel system, which can ruin injectors and lines. Water or poor-quality fuel makes failure more likely.
issues.next: Drain the water separator and change fuel filters on schedule. If the truck stalls or will not restart, have it towed rather than cranking it over and over.

issues.t: Rough or erratic automatic shifting
issues.sym: Harsh or delayed shifts, slipping, sudden large downshifts, or the transmission dropping out of gear.
issues.why: The first year of this generation drew a cluster of owner complaints about its six-speed automatic, including slipping and incorrect gear changes.
issues.next: Have the transmission scanned for codes, check the fluid, and ask about software updates. Get it checked promptly if it slips or drops into neutral.

issues.t: Driveshaft damper can slip and break the driveshaft (recall)
issues.sym: A new vibration, clunk or rattle from under the truck that gets worse with speed.
issues.why: A balancing damper on the driveshaft of some 4x4 trucks can move out of place, unbalancing the shaft until it cracks. Ford recalled affected trucks.
issues.next: Check the VIN for the open recall and stop driving to have the driveshaft inspected if a new vibration appears.

issues.t: Tailgate can open on its own (recall)
issues.sym: The tailgate drops open while driving or parked, sometimes after rain or a car wash.
issues.why: Water can get into the wiring for the electric tailgate release switch and short it, which releases the latches. Ford recalled affected trucks.
issues.next: Look up the VIN for the recall and do not carry loose cargo in the bed until it is repaired.

issues.t: Fuel pump deposits can cause stalling (recall)
issues.sym: Power loss, fuel-pressure warnings, stalling while driving, or a no-start.
issues.why: Deposits can form on parts inside the high-pressure fuel pump, linked to biodiesel blends. Ford recalled affected trucks and later reopened the campaign for some that were repaired incorrectly.
issues.next: Check the VIN for both recalls, even if work was done before. If the truck loses power, get off the road and have it towed.

issues.t: 360-degree camera rear image too dark or washed out (recall)
issues.sym: The backup camera picture is badly under- or over-exposed in certain lighting, making it hard to see behind the truck.
issues.why: On trucks with the 360-degree camera system, exposure software can mis-adjust the image when the cameras see very different light. Ford recalled affected trucks for a software update.
issues.next: Have the image module software updated under the recall, and use mirrors and look back when reversing until then.

issues.t: Steering column shaft bolts may be loose or missing (recall)
issues.sym: A clunk or extra free play in the steering wheel, or steering that feels disconnected.
issues.why: Bolts at the upper steering shaft coupler may have been left out or not tightened at the factory, so the column could separate. Ford recalled affected trucks.
issues.next: Do not drive if the steering feels loose. Check the VIN and have the recall done right away.

issues.t: Rear axle shaft may break (recall)
issues.sym: Grinding or clunking from the rear axle, loss of drive, or the truck rolling while in Park without the parking brake set.
issues.why: The left rear axle shaft on some single-rear-wheel trucks may not have been heat-treated correctly and can fracture. Ford recalled affected trucks.
issues.next: Always set the parking brake and check the VIN for the recall. Stop driving if rear-axle grinding or clunking starts.

issues.t: Infotainment screen can block the backup camera (recall)
issues.sym: When shifting into Reverse, the home screen stays up instead of the rear camera image.
issues.why: A software error can keep the center screen from switching to the rearview camera. Ford recalled affected trucks.
issues.next: Check the VIN for the recall and have the software updated. Use mirrors and look back while reversing until it is fixed.

issues.t: Analog gauges may stick or read wrong (recall)
issues.sym: The speedometer or tachometer needle sticks, jumps or reads incorrectly.
issues.why: A fault in the analog instrument cluster can make the gauge needles move erratically. Ford recalled affected trucks.
issues.next: Check the VIN for the recall. Do not rely on a jumping speedometer; have it repaired promptly.

issues.t: LED headlights may fail (recall)
issues.sym: A headlight goes dim, flickers or stops working.
issues.why: Some headlight assemblies may have a contaminated LED chip, which can cause the light to fail. Ford recalled affected trucks.
issues.next: Check the VIN for the recall and avoid night driving with a failed headlight until it is replaced.

issues.t: Tailgate support cable may break under load (recall)
issues.sym: The tailgate drops or hangs crooked when weight is put on it.
issues.why: The left-side tailgate cable may fail under heavy loads and let the tailgate fall. Ford recalled affected trucks.
issues.next: Do not load or stand on the open tailgate until the recall is done.

issues.t: Right rear axle shaft may break (recall)
issues.sym: Grinding or clunking from the rear axle, loss of drive, or the truck rolling while in Park without the parking brake set.
issues.why: The right rear axle shaft on some trucks may not have been made correctly and can fracture. Ford recalled affected trucks.
issues.next: Always set the parking brake and check the VIN for the recall. Stop driving if rear-axle grinding or clunking starts.

issues.t: Spark plugs seize and break during removal
issues.sym: No symptom while driving. The trouble appears at tune-up time, when one or more spark plugs snap and leave the lower half stuck in the cylinder head.
issues.why: The original two-piece spark plugs on these 3-valve engines collect carbon around a long lower sleeve, which can lock the plug in the head so it separates when turned. Ford published a special removal procedure and extraction tool, and later engines got a redesigned head.
issues.next: Nothing urgent. When plugs are due, use a shop that knows the Ford procedure and has the extraction tool, and replace them with the updated one-piece design.

issues.t: Turbocharger failure on early 6.7L diesels
issues.sym: A loud screech or siren-like whine from the engine, a drop in power, and blue-white smoke from the tailpipe as the turbo passes oil.
issues.why: The first turbochargers on this engine used ceramic ball bearings that could break up. Ford later changed to steel bearings, which largely ended the problem.
issues.next: Stop driving if the turbo starts screeching or the truck smokes heavily, because a failing turbo can send oil and debris into the engine. Have a diesel shop inspect it and fit the updated turbo.

issues.t: NOx sensor failure triggers reduced power
issues.sym: A check engine light or exhaust fluid system warning, sometimes with a countdown to limited speed or noticeably reduced power.
issues.why: The sensors that measure nitrogen oxides in the exhaust failed often on early trucks, and the computer cuts power when it cannot confirm the emissions system is working. Ford ran a customer program on 2011 trucks to replace sensors and update the software.
issues.next: Have the codes read soon so the truck does not drop into a speed-limited mode. Ask a Ford dealer whether the sensor and software update were done on your truck.

issues.t: Camshaft position sensor failure
issues.sym: The engine cranks but will not start, or it stumbles, cuts out, or stalls while driving, often with the tachometer dropping out.
issues.why: The cam sensor tells the engine computer when to fire the injectors. It is a known weak point on this engine and can fail or work intermittently.
issues.next: Have the sensor tested and replaced; it is a fairly simple repair. Carrying a spare is a common owner habit on these trucks.

issues.t: Underbody insulator can wear through the aluminum driveshaft
issues.sym: A vibration that builds with speed, a clunk from under the floor, and in the worst case a loud bang and loss of drive.
issues.why: A heat insulator under the body can sit against the aluminum driveshaft and rub a groove in it until the tube is too thin to hold torque.
issues.next: Stop driving and have the driveshaft and insulator inspected right away under the recall, because a broken shaft can drop and dig into the road.
